docs.title: Philter Diffuse
docs.text: Philter Diffuse releases PII count aggregations with differential privacy, using OpenDP. It is designed for organizations that need to share or publish aggregate statistics about personally identifiable information (PII) with a formal bound on how much a release reveals about any one document.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In many data analysis scenarios, simply removing direct identifiers (like names) is insufficient to protect privacy. Aggregate counts can still leak information if an attacker has background knowledge or if the counts are very small. Philter Diffuse addresses this by applying Differential Privacy, a rigorous mathematical framework for privacy protection.

It uses the Discrete Laplace mechanism to privatize PII counts. This mechanism adds carefully calibrated random noise to the raw counts, so that the presence or absence of any single document has a limited impact on the released results.

The protected unit is one document: one redaction in Philter, or one record counted by the source. A person who appears in many documents can move a count by as many documents as they appear in, and their protection weakens in proportion: epsilon times that number.

docs.title: Integration with the Philter Ecosystem
docs.text:
Philter Diffuse is a key component of the Philterd privacy suite, designed to work seamlessly with:

  • Philter: A PII detection and redaction engine. Philter identifies PII in unstructured text.
  • Phileas: The PII redaction library underneath Philter, for Java, Python, and .NET.

Typically, Philter redacts text and records counts of the PII types it found. Philter Diffuse then takes these raw counts and applies differential privacy before they are used for reporting or analytics. An application using Phileas directly can write its own counts to a JSON file for Philter Diffuse.

docs.title: Get Started
docs.text: New to Philter Diffuse? The Quickstart takes you from a clean checkout to a privatized CSV and an audit report in about five minutes, no database required. For the current release state and maturity, see Project Status.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Robust Differential Privacy: Implements the Discrete Laplace mechanism from the OpenDP library, with a formal bound on how much a release reveals about any one document.
  • Declared PII Types: Releases only the types you list, so the output does not reveal which types the data holds.
  • Persistent Privacy Budget Management: Tracks the cumulative "epsilon" (privacy loss) across multiple queries. This prevents "privacy exhaustion," where repeated queries on the same data could eventually reveal individual information.
  • Flexible Data Ingestion:
    • MongoDB Integration: Directly connect to MongoDB to fetch and privatize counts stored in collections.
    • JSON Support: Process PII counts from simple local JSON files, making it easy to integrate into existing pipelines.
  • Audit Reports: Prints a report for every execution, with the epsilon spent and a qualitative interpretation of the privacy strength (e.g., "EXTREME", "HIGH").
  • Safe Output Formatting:
    • CSV Export: Results are exported to standard CSV format for easy consumption by downstream tools.
    • Thresholding: Automatically suppresses counts below a user-defined threshold (e.g., showing "None" for counts less than 5) to provide an additional layer of protection against re-identification.
  • Reads Philter Telemetry Directly: Privatizes Philter's aggregated, document-presence PII counts with --aggregates, read through Philter's API with an API key (--philter-url, Philter 4.0 or later) or from its pii_count_aggregates collection (deprecated), so you can run analytics on your own redaction telemetry.
  • Dockerized Deployment: Easily deployable via Docker for consistent and isolated execution environments.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
docs.text: This page addresses common questions and concerns regarding Philter Diffuse, its implementation of differential privacy, and its integration into your data pipelines.

docs.title: What is Philter Diffuse?
docs.text: Philter Diffuse is a specialized utility designed to add an extra layer of privacy to PII (Personally Identifiable Information) count aggregations. By using the Discrete Laplace mechanism provided by the OpenDP library, it injects mathematical noise into raw counts, bounding how much the aggregate output reveals about any one document.

docs.title: When would I use Philter Diffuse?
docs.text: You would use Philter Diffuse when you need to report or share statistics based on sensitive PII (Personally Identifiable Information) but need to limit what those statistics reveal about any one document in the dataset. This is common in healthcare, financial reporting, and academic research where aggregate data must be publicly released or shared with third parties.

docs.title: How does it differ from "standard" anonymization?
docs.text: Traditional anonymization (like k-anonymity) often fails against linkage attacks or background knowledge. Differential privacy provides a formal bound on how much the presence or absence of a single document can change the outcome of the analysis.

docs.title: Does it protect people or documents?
docs.text: Documents. The bound applies to one document: one redaction in Philter, or one record counted by the source. A person who appears in many documents can move a count by as many documents as they appear in, and their protection weakens in proportion: epsilon times that number. Philter's counts do not identify people, so Philter Diffuse cannot limit how much one person contributes. Account for this when you choose --scale and --budget-ceiling, particularly where one person can appear in many documents.

docs.title: Why must I list the PII types?
docs.text: A row for each type found would show that at least one document held that type, even with its count masked as None. With --pii-types, the rows are fixed before the data is read. See Choosing the PII types.

docs.title: Is commercial support available?
docs.text: Yes. Commercial support for Philter Diffuse is available through Philterd, LLC. We offer enterprise-grade service level agreements (SLAs), custom integration assistance, and priority bug fixes for our entire ecosystem of PII de-identification tools.

docs.title: Is Philter Diffuse part of a larger ecosystem?
docs.text: Yes. Philter Diffuse is designed to complement Philter (the PII de-identification engine) and Phileas (the PII redaction library underneath Philter). While Philter removes PII from text, Philter Diffuse ensures that the statistics derived from that PII remain private.

docs.title: What is the "Epsilon" ($\epsilon$) value?
docs.text: Epsilon is a measure of "privacy loss." A smaller epsilon (e.g., 0.1) means more privacy but less accuracy because more noise is added. A larger epsilon (e.g., 5.0) means less privacy but higher accuracy. Philter Diffuse calculates epsilon as $n / \text{scale}$, where $n$ is the number of PII types in --pii-types.

docs.title: Why are some counts returned as "None"?
docs.text: When you set a --threshold (e.g., --threshold 10), any privatized count that falls below that value is masked as None. This prevents the leakage of information from very small cohorts, which are often the most vulnerable to re-identification.

docs.title: Can the privatized counts be negative?
docs.text: Mathematically, Laplace noise can be negative and could result in a negative count. However, Philter Diffuse automatically clips all privatized counts to a minimum of 0 to ensure the output is realistic for count-based data.

docs.title: What is "Sensitivity"?
docs.text: Sensitivity is how much adding or removing one document can change the released counts. Philter Diffuse counts documents, so one document changes any one count by at most 1. A document can contain several PII types, though, and so change several counts at once: the sensitivity of a query is the number of PII types in --pii-types.

docs.title: Why do I need a "Budget Ceiling"?
docs.text: If you run the same query multiple times on the same data, an attacker could potentially average the results to filter out the noise and find the true value. The privacy budget (managed via --budget-ceiling) tracks the cumulative epsilon spent and stops providing accurate results once the limit is reached to prevent this "averaging attack."

docs.title: Where is the budget stored?
docs.text:
• MongoDB Mode: The budget is stored in a collection named privacy_metadata within your database.
  • Philter API Mode (--philter-url): The budget is stored in the budget file, keyed by the Philter URL. Nothing is written to Philter's database.
  • JSON Mode: The budget is stored in the budget file, keyed by the --source name.

The budget file is ~/.philter-diffuse/privacy_budget.json, unless --budget-file or the PHILTER_DIFFUSE_BUDGET_FILE environment variable names another.

docs.title: How can I reset the privacy budget?
docs.text: In a development or testing environment, reset the budget as follows. In production, see Resetting the Budget first. * In MongoDB: Drop the privacy_metadata collection or delete the specific document for your collection. * In JSON or Philter API mode: Remove the entry from the budget file, or delete the file. * Note: In production, resetting the budget should be done with extreme caution as it potentially invalidates the privacy bound on the underlying documents.

docs.title: Why did my run stop with a budget error?
docs.text: The release would have taken cumulative privacy loss past the --budget-ceiling. To protect the data, Philter Diffuse exits with an error (exit code 1), writes no output, leaves any existing --output file unchanged, and spends no budget. The error gives the cost of the release and the amount already spent.

docs.title: My MongoDB connection is failing. What should I check?
docs.text: Ensure that your --mongo-uri is correct and follows the format mongodb://[user:pass@]host:port/database. Also, verify that the MongoDB instance is accessible from the environment where Philter Diffuse is running (check firewalls and network bindings).

docs.title: Can I use Philter Diffuse with other databases besides MongoDB?
docs.text: Currently, Philter Diffuse has native support for MongoDB, local JSON files, and Philter's PII Counts API (--philter-url, Philter 4.0 or later). For other databases, we recommend exporting your PII counts to a JSON format and using the --input flag.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Philter Diffuse runs from its Docker image, or from a checkout of its repository with Python. It is not published to PyPI.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before installing Philter Diffuse, ensure your system meets the following requirements:

  • Python: Version 3.12 is tested, in CI and in the Docker image. The current OpenDP release requires 3.10 or later.
  • pip: The standard Python package manager.
  • MongoDB (Optional): If you plan to use MongoDB as a data source, ensure it's installed and accessible from your environment.
  • Docker (Optional): If you prefer to run the application in a container.

docs.title: Direct Installation
docs.text:
1. Clone the Repository: bash git clone https://github.com/philterd/philter-diffuse.git cd philter-diffuse

  2. Create a Virtual Environment (Recommended): It's best practice to use a virtual environment to manage dependencies and avoid conflicts with other projects. bash python -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate # On macOS/Linux # venv\Scripts\activate # On Windows

  3. Install Dependencies: The core dependencies for Philter Diffuse include opendp, pymongo, and other support libraries. Install them using the provided requirements.txt: bash pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Docker Installation
docs.text: Docker provides an isolated and consistent environment for running Philter Diffuse, eliminating potential "it works on my machine" issues.

docs.title: 1. Get the Docker Image
docs.text:
Pull the image from Docker Hub:

docker pull philterd/philter-diffuse:0.1.0

To build it from a checkout instead, run this from the root of the project directory, and use philter-diffuse as the image name in the commands below:

docker build -t philter-diffuse .

docs.title: 2. Run the Container
docs.text:
You can run the container manually, or from a checkout use the provided run-docker.sh script, which builds the image and automates common volume mounts for data processing.

Example: Using the provided script

./run-docker.sh

Example: Running manually with volume mounts The image's entrypoint is main.py, so arguments after the image name are Philter Diffuse's options. It runs in /data, and the image sets PHILTER_DIFFUSE_BUDGET_FILE to /data/privacy_budget.json: mount a directory there to hold the input, the output, and the budget.

docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v $(pwd)/data:/data \
           philterd/philter-diffuse:0.1.0 \
           --input pii_counts.json \
           --source claims-2026 \
           --pii-types ssn,age,zipcode,creditcard \
           --output privatized_counts.csv

The image runs as an unprivileged user (UID 1000), not root. --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" runs it as you, so it can write to a directory you own. A Docker named volume needs no --user.

Always mount /data. The spent privacy budget is kept in /data/privacy_budget.json, so without the mount it is lost when the container exits and the next run starts with a fresh budget, which defeats --budget-ceiling.

Example: Reading counts from a Philter container To read counts from a Philter container through its API (Philter 4.0 or later), attach both containers to one Docker network and address Philter by its alias philter, which is in the subject alternative name of the self-signed certificate Philter's image generates. Export that certificate into data/ first (see Usage).

docker network create philter-net
docker network connect --alias philter philter-net <philter-container>
docker run --rm --network philter-net --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v $(pwd)/data:/data \
           -e PHILTER_API_KEY \
           philterd/philter-diffuse:0.1.0 \
           --philter-url https://philter:8080 \
           --philter-ca-cert philter.pem \
           --pii-types ssn,email-address,phone-number \
           --output privatized_counts.csv

-e PHILTER_API_KEY passes the key from your shell's environment without putting it on the command line. The budget is keyed by the URL, so keep using the same --philter-url for a deployment: https://philter:8080 and https://localhost:8080 are separate budget entries.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After installation, verify that Philter Diffuse is ready to use by running the help command:

python main.py --help

You should see a list of available command-line options and their descriptions.

docs.title: Privacy Budget Management
docs.text: Differential privacy relies on the concept of a "privacy budget," typically denoted by the Greek letter epsilon ($\epsilon$). This budget represents the maximum cumulative privacy loss that an organization is willing to tolerate for a given dataset. It is measured per document: a person who appears in many documents loses up to epsilon times that number.

docs.title: The Core Concept: Epsilon ($\epsilon$)
docs.text:
In Philter Diffuse, $\epsilon$ is a measure of the information leak allowed for each query.

  • Calculation: For the Discrete Laplace mechanism used here, epsilon for a single query is calculated as: $$\epsilon = \frac{\Delta f}{\text{scale}}$$ Where $\Delta f$ is the sensitivity and scale is the noise parameter provided by the user via --scale. One document adds at most one to each PII type's count, but it can add to every type at once, so the sensitivity of a query is the number of PII types in --pii-types. The charge depends on that list, not on which types the data holds. OpenDP computes epsilon from it.
  • Default: With the default scale of 2.0, a query releasing 4 PII types consumes $\epsilon = 4/2 = 2.0$. To spend less per query, raise --scale: epsilon falls in proportion.

docs.title: Why do we need a budget?
docs.text: Every time a privatized query is released, a small amount of information about the underlying data is leaked. If an attacker can query the same dataset multiple times with different noise, they could potentially average out the noise to reconstruct the original values. A privacy budget places a hard limit on this cumulative leakage.

docs.title: Persistent Tracking
docs.text:
Philter Diffuse automatically tracks the cumulative epsilon spent for each unique data source (a MongoDB collection, a JSON file, or a Philter deployment read through its API). This tracking is persistent, meaning it survives between different executions of the tool.

  • MongoDB Mode: The spent budget is stored in a collection named privacy_metadata within the same database as the data.
  • JSON Mode: The spent budget is stored in the budget file, under the --source name. A renamed or copied input file keeps its budget, and a new --source name starts a new one, so use one name per dataset.
  • Philter API Mode (--philter-url): The spent budget is stored in the budget file, under a key naming the Philter URL, such as pii_count_aggregates@https://localhost:8080. Nothing is written to Philter or its database. Every read from that deployment draws on the one budget, whatever --context, --from, or --to it uses, so overlapping reports cannot each spend a fresh budget. If Philter reports that count recording is off, no budget is spent. Moving from --mongo-uri --aggregates to --philter-url starts a new budget entry: the epsilon already spent is recorded in MongoDB's privacy_metadata collection (under the pii_counts collection name), not in the budget file. When you move, copy the spent epsilon to the new entry so earlier releases still count against the ceiling.

The budget file is ~/.philter-diffuse/privacy_budget.json, so it does not depend on the working directory. To keep it elsewhere, such as on storage shared by several machines, set --budget-file or the PHILTER_DIFFUSE_BUDGET_FILE environment variable, and use the same file for every run against a source. A budget file that cannot be read stops the run rather than starting again from zero, so back it up.

The budget is charged before any noise is sampled, as one step with the ceiling check, so runs at the same time cannot each spend the same balance. On Windows, concurrent runs against one budget file are not serialized: run them one at a time.

docs.title: The Budget Ceiling
docs.text: The --budget-ceiling parameter (default: 10.0) defines the maximum allowed cumulative epsilon.

docs.title: What happens when the ceiling is reached?
docs.text:
If a requested query would cause the total spent epsilon to exceed the ceiling, Philter Diffuse refuses it:

  1. Error: The run exits with code 1, and standard error gives the cost of the release and the amount already spent.
  2. No Output: No counts are released. Any existing --output file is left unchanged, and no report is printed.
  3. No Budget Consumption: Nothing is deducted from the remaining budget.

docs.title: Interpreting Protection Strength
docs.text:
To assist non-technical auditors, Philter Diffuse provides a qualitative interpretation of the privacy loss of each query (not the cumulative total, which is in the budget store):

Query Epsilon ($\epsilon$) Protection Strength Description $\epsilon \leq 0.1$ EXTREME Highest level of protection; suitable for extremely sensitive data. $0.1 < \epsilon \leq 1.0$ HIGH Strong protection; standard for most production use cases. $1.0 < \epsilon \leq 5.0$ MODERATE Balanced protection and utility. $\epsilon > 5.0$ LOW Useful for testing or less sensitive data; more can be inferred about any one document.

docs.title: Resetting the Budget
docs.text:
The budget covers every document in a source, and it does not renew. Resetting it is sound only when later releases leave out every document an earlier release covered. A release of new data that still includes the old data adds to the privacy loss of the old documents, so resetting the budget before it removes the protection the ceiling provides.

  • Philter API: Philter's counts accumulate, so a read without --from and --to includes every earlier day. After a reset, limit every release with --from to days after the last release. Philter Diffuse does not check this.
  • JSON: A dataset with no documents in common with an earlier one needs no reset: give it a new --source name.

The bound stays per document, so a person who appears in documents on both sides of a reset is exposed to both sets of releases.

To reset the budget: * MongoDB: Delete the document for that collection in the privacy_metadata collection. * JSON or Philter API: Edit the budget file and remove the entry for your --source name or Philter URL, or delete the file entirely.

docs.title: Adjusting the Ceiling
docs.text: You can increase the ceiling by passing a higher value to the --budget-ceiling flag during execution. However, this should only be done after careful consideration of the privacy implications.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This walkthrough takes you from a clean checkout to a privatized CSV and a privacy audit report in about five minutes. It uses JSON mode, so you do not need MongoDB.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/philterd/philter-diffuse.git
cd philter-diffuse
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate            # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

Confirm the tool runs:

python main.py --version

docs.title: 2. Create some input counts
docs.text:
Philter Diffuse privatizes counts of PII entities. These usually come from the PII counts Philter records, but for this quickstart create a small JSON file by hand. Save the following as pii_counts.json:

{
  "ssn": 8,
  "creditcard": 15,
  "age": 120,
  "zipcode": 45,
  "date": 3
}

The keys are PII types and the values are raw counts (for example, 8 documents contained an SSN).

docs.title: 3. Run the privatization
docs.text:
python main.py \
  --input pii_counts.json \
  --source quickstart \
  --output privatized_counts.csv \
  --pii-types ssn,creditcard,age,zipcode,date \
  --scale 2.0 \
  --threshold 5

What each flag does:

  • --input reads the raw counts from your JSON file.
  • --source names the dataset. The privacy budget is tracked under this name, so renaming the file does not reset it.
  • --output writes the differentially private counts to a CSV.
  • --pii-types names the types to release. The output has exactly these rows whether or not the input holds each type, so choose the list before looking at the counts.
  • --scale 2.0 sets the noise level. Each listed PII type costs 1 / scale, because one document can add to every type at once, so these five types spend 5 / 2.0 = 2.5.
  • --threshold 5 masks any privatized count below 5 as None, protecting small cohorts.

docs.title: 4. Read the audit report
docs.text:
The tool prints a privacy audit report to the console. Because the noise is random, your numbers will differ slightly each run:

========================================
PRIVACY AUDIT REPORT
========================================
Privacy Loss (Epsilon): 2.5000
Protection Strength:   MODERATE
Influence Limit:      e^2.50 (12.18x)
Output File:          privatized_counts.csv
Count Threshold:      5
----------------------------------------
PII Type        | Private
----------------------------------------
ssn             | 9
creditcard      | 14
age             | 122
zipcode         | 49
date            | None
----------------------------------------
  • Privacy Loss (Epsilon) is the budget spent by this query.
  • Protection Strength is a plain-language reading of epsilon (MODERATE here). Raise --scale for stronger protection: --scale 10 spends 0.5 on these five types.
  • The table shows the private counts, the same values as the CSV. The report never prints raw counts, so it is safe in logs.
  • date shows None because its privatized count fell below the threshold of 5.

docs.title: 5. Inspect the CSV
docs.text:
cat privatized_counts.csv

PII Type,Private Count
ssn,9
creditcard,14
age,122
zipcode,49
date,None

This CSV is the artifact you can hand to analysts, auditors, or a downstream dashboard.

docs.title: 6. Watch the privacy budget
docs.text:
Philter Diffuse remembers how much epsilon you have spent against each source. Run the same command again and look at the budget file it created:

cat ~/.philter-diffuse/privacy_budget.json

{"quickstart": 5.0}

Two runs at --scale 2.0 have spent 2.5 + 2.5 = 5.0. The default ceiling is 10.0; once cumulative epsilon would cross it, Philter Diffuse refuses the run: it exits with an error and writes no output. See Privacy Budget Management for how to manage and reset the budget.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Read counts straight from MongoDB, or Philter's recorded PII counts through its API, in Usage.
  • Understand epsilon, the ceiling, and budget exhaustion in Privacy Budget Management.
  • Check the release state and maturity in Project Status.

docs.title: Release state
docs.text:
Philter Diffuse is early-access software at version 0.1.0.

The differential-privacy mechanism (Discrete Laplace via OpenDP), the privacy-budget accounting, and the command-line interface are usable and covered by tests. Because it is a 0.x release, the command-line interface and output format may still change before a stable 1.0. Pin to a specific commit or release if you depend on the current behavior.

Check the version of your checkout at any time:

python main.py --version

This is the authoritative status for the product. Marketing or product-page copy should defer to the version and checklist here rather than implying a stable release exists before one is tagged.

docs.title: Maturity checklist
docs.text:
The current state of the things a developer-facing tool needs before it is "done":

Area State Notes Tests Done test_main.py exercises privatization, budget tracking, thresholding, JSON/Mongo ingestion, the aggregates reader, and reading counts from Philter's API against a stubbed Philter; CI runs pytest on every push and pull request (.github/workflows/tests.yml). Examples Done example.sh (local JSON run) and run-docker.sh (containerized run) are runnable end to end; the Quickstart is a worked walkthrough. Docs Done Install, usage, CLI options, privacy-budget management, quickstart, and FAQ are published to https://philterd.github.io/philter-diffuse/ and rebuilt on every push (.github/workflows/docs.yml). Release artifact Done 0.1.0 is tagged, with a GitHub release and a Docker image, philterd/philter-diffuse, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Philter Diffuse is not packaged for PyPI.

When the checklist items change, update this table and the __version__ in main.py together.

docs.title: Roadmap to 1.0
docs.text: • Freeze the CLI flags and CSV schema, then promote to 1.0.0.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Philter Diffuse is a command-line tool designed to process PII counts and apply differential privacy. It reads counts from a MongoDB database, a local JSON file, or Philter's API. Each run names exactly one source: --mongo-uri, --input, or --philter-url.

docs.title: 1. MongoDB Mode
docs.text:
In this mode, Philter Diffuse connects to a MongoDB instance, counts the documents in the pii_counts collection of the database named in the URI that have each field listed in --pii-types, and privatizes those counts. This mode is not tied to Philter; to read Philter's counts, see Reading Philter's PII counts.

Example Command:

python main.py --mongo-uri "mongodb://localhost:27017/analytics_db" --pii-types ssn,age,zipcode --output results.csv
  • Behavior: It connects to the analytics_db on localhost.
  • Fields: The tool counts documents containing each field in --pii-types. The collection is fixed.
  • Access: The MongoDB user needs write access to the privacy_metadata collection, where the budget is kept. A run by a read-only user stops with an error and releases nothing.

docs.title: 2. JSON Mode
docs.text:
If you already have a JSON file containing the counts of various PII types, you can provide it directly using the --input flag. This is ideal for integration with existing logging or data pipeline tools.

Example Command:

python main.py --input data/pii_counts.json --source claims-2026 --pii-types ssn,age,zipcode,creditcard,email --output results.csv

--source names the dataset. The privacy budget is tracked under that name, so a renamed or copied file keeps its budget. Use the same name for every release from one dataset.

Expected JSON Format: The JSON file must be a flat object where keys represent the PII type and values are whole counts of 0 or more. Any other value stops the run with an error before anything is released or charged.

{
  "ssn": 105,
  "age": 450,
  "zipcode": 122,
  "creditcard": 58,
  "email": 210
}

docs.title: Choosing the PII types
docs.text:
--pii-types is required. Philter Diffuse releases exactly the types you list, in that order, so the rows of the output cannot reveal which types the data holds. A row for each type found would show that at least one document held that type, even with its count masked as None, and no epsilon bounds that disclosure.

  • Choose the list before looking at the counts, from your redaction policy or from what your report needs. Choosing it from the counts brings the disclosure back. Keep the list the same between releases.
  • Each type costs 1 / scale, whether or not the source holds it, because one document can add to every listed type at once. List only the types you need.
  • A listed type the source does not hold is counted as 0 and receives noise like any other.
  • Types not listed are left out of the release. A warning on standard error gives how many, without their names, so a misspelled type does not go unnoticed. Names must match the source exactly. Philter uses its filter type names, such as ssn, email-address, phone-number, credit-card, and person.

docs.title: Command Line Options
docs.text:
Flag Description Default --input Path to a local JSON file containing PII counts. None --source Required with --input. A name for the dataset the counts come from, which the privacy budget is tracked under. None --mongo-uri The connection string for your MongoDB instance. None --pii-types [Required] The PII types to release, comma-separated, such as ssn,email-address. Output has one row per type whether or not the source holds it, and types not listed are left out. Each type costs 1 / scale of epsilon. See Choosing the PII types. None --scale The scale parameter for the Laplace noise. A higher scale adds more noise (more privacy, less accuracy). 2.0 --output [Required] The file path where the privatized CSV results will be saved. None --threshold Results with a privatized count below this value will be masked as None in the output. 0 --budget-ceiling The maximum cumulative privacy budget (epsilon) allowed for a single source. 10.0 --budget-file Where to keep the privacy budget, for sources other than MongoDB. PHILTER_DIFFUSE_BUDGET_FILE, then ~/.philter-diffuse/privacy_budget.json --aggregates Read Philter's aggregated, document-presence PII counts instead of counting documents per field. With --philter-url they are read through Philter's API; otherwise from the pii_count_aggregates collection in MongoDB (deprecated). off --context When using --aggregates, restrict to Philter contexts of this name. Through Philter's API, contexts of that name belong to the API key's user unless Philter's ADMIN_CROSS_USER_ACCESS_ENABLED is on, when they include every user's. all contexts --philter-url Read the aggregates through Philter's API (Philter 4.0 or later) at this URL, such as https://localhost:8080. Implies --aggregates. The API key is read from the PHILTER_API_KEY environment variable. None --philter-ca-cert With --philter-url, a PEM file holding a certificate to trust in addition to the system's certificate authorities, such as Philter's self-signed certificate. None --from With --philter-url, read only counts for this UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD) or later. None --to With --philter-url, read only counts for this UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD) or earlier. None --version Print the Philter Diffuse version and exit.

Run python main.py --help to see this list from the tool itself. A flag that does not apply to the chosen source is refused with exit code 2 rather than ignored.

docs.title: 3. Reading Philter's PII counts (--aggregates)
docs.text: When Philter is configured to record PII count statistics (its diffuseCountsEnabled admin setting, off by default), it records document-presence counts: one entry per user's (context, day), each holding a map of {pii_type: number-of-documents-containing-it}. Instead of counting documents field by field, point Philter Diffuse at those counts directly. Philter Diffuse sums the entries into a single {pii_type: total} map and privatizes that. Because each redaction contributes at most one to any type's count (document presence), summing across entries keeps each count's sensitivity at 1. A document can contain several types, so a query's epsilon is the number of types released divided by --scale.

docs.title: Through Philter's API (recommended)
docs.text:
Philter 4.0 and later serve the counts at GET /api/pii-counts. Reading them there needs only a Philter API key: no network access to or credentials for Philter's database, and no dependence on how Philter stores the counts.

export PHILTER_API_KEY=<api key>
python main.py --philter-url https://localhost:8080 --pii-types ssn,email-address,phone-number --output privatized_counts.csv

--philter-url implies --aggregates. Narrow the counts by context and by UTC day (both dates inclusive):

python main.py --philter-url https://localhost:8080 --pii-types ssn,email-address,phone-number \
  --context claims-intake --from 2026-09-01 --to 2026-09-30 --output privatized_counts.csv

Philter applies these filters itself, and Philter Diffuse reads every page of the result before summing.

The API key. Philter Diffuse reads the key only from the PHILTER_API_KEY environment variable, never from a command-line argument, so it does not appear in shell history or process listings. It never prints the key. Because the counts cover the whole Philter deployment, the key must hold the pii-counts:read scope and its user must be a Philter administrator. Philter records every read in its audit log.

When recording is off. If Philter reports that count recording is turned off, Philter Diffuse says so and exits with status 1 without writing privatized output or spending privacy budget. An empty result in that state does not mean Philter found no PII, so it is not privatized as if it did. An administrator turns recording on with Philter's Settings API ({"diffuseCountsEnabled": true}).

When Philter refuses. A refusal is reported with Philter's HTTP status and reason code, a hint for the common ones, and Philter's request ID (from its X-Request-Id header) so the request can be found in Philter's audit log:

Error: Philter refused the request (HTTP 403, missing_scope): This API key does not have the 'pii-counts:read' scope. The API key needs the pii-counts:read scope. (Philter request ID: 01929f2e-6c3a-7b1d-9e4f-3a2b1c0d9e8f)
reason What to do invalid_credentials PHILTER_API_KEY is missing, mistyped, or revoked. missing_scope Give the key the pii-counts:read scope. admin_required Use a key whose user is a Philter administrator. HTTP 404 Philter is older than 4.0, or --philter-url points somewhere else. HTTP 400 with no reason With an http:// URL, Philter is most likely serving HTTPS on that port. Use https://.

TLS. Certificates are verified, and verification cannot be turned off. Philter's Docker image generates a self-signed certificate (with localhost, philter, and 127.0.0.1 in its subject alternative name) the first time it starts. To trust it, export it as PEM (the keystore password is SSL_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, philter by default) and pass it with --philter-ca-cert:

docker cp <philter-container>:/opt/philter/ssl/philter.p12 .
openssl pkcs12 -in philter.p12 -clcerts -nokeys -passin pass:philter -out philter.pem
python main.py --philter-url https://localhost:8080 --philter-ca-cert philter.pem --pii-types ssn,email-address,phone-number --output privatized_counts.csv

--philter-ca-cert adds to the system's certificate authorities, so it also takes a private CA's certificate. Where TLS is terminated in front of Philter and Philter serves plain HTTP, use an http:// URL only over a private network: the API key travels in every request. Redirects are not followed, so the key is only ever sent to the URL you give.

Privacy budget. The budget for API reads is tracked in the budget file, keyed by the Philter URL, not in Philter's database. Moving from the MongoDB path starts a new budget entry, so carry the epsilon already spent over to it; see Privacy Budget Management.

docs.title: From MongoDB (deprecated)
docs.text:
Philter Diffuse can still read the pii_count_aggregates collection from Philter's MongoDB:

python main.py --mongo-uri "mongodb://localhost:27017/philter" --aggregates --pii-types ssn,email-address,phone-number --output privatized_counts.csv

Restrict to one Philter context with --context. This path is deprecated: it prints a warning naming --philter-url, and it will be removed in a future release. It needs network access and credentials for Philter's database, works only when Philter uses MongoDB storage, and depends on Philter's internal collection layout. Move to --philter-url once you run Philter 4.0 or later. --from and --to are only available with --philter-url.

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text: Philter Diffuse provides two forms of output for every execution:

docs.title: 1. Privatized CSV File
docs.text:
The file specified by the --output flag will contain a list of PII types and their corresponding privatized counts. For the JSON example above, run with --threshold 60:

python main.py --input data/pii_counts.json --source claims-2026 --pii-types ssn,age,zipcode,creditcard,email --output results.csv --threshold 60

Example CSV Content:

PII Type,Private Count
ssn,108
age,451
zipcode,122
creditcard,None
email,213

Note: creditcard is "None" because its privatized count fell below the threshold of 60.

docs.title: 2. Privacy Audit Report
docs.text:
A human-readable report is printed to the standard output (stdout) summarizing the execution and the privacy bound applied.

Key Report Sections: * Privacy Loss (Epsilon): The specific amount of privacy budget consumed by this particular execution (the number of PII types released divided by --scale). * Protection Strength: A qualitative assessment of the privacy level (e.g., "HIGH" or "MODERATE"). * Influence Limit: A mathematical multiplier representing the maximum change one document can have on the output probability. * Private Counts Table: The privatized count for each PII type, as written to the CSV. Raw counts are never printed, so the report can go to container or CI logs.

docs.title: Using the Output in BI Tools
docs.text:
Load the CSV into a BI tool, such as Metabase or Tableau, as you would any other table. A released CSV can be read, shared, and refreshed on a dashboard as often as needed at no further privacy cost, because reusing a released result spends no budget.

Do not point a dashboard refresh at Philter Diffuse itself. Every run is a new release that spends budget, so regenerate the CSV only when you mean to publish new numbers.

docs.title: Practical Example: Increasing Privacy
docs.text:
If you are dealing with extremely sensitive data and want to increase the privacy protection, increase the --scale parameter:

python main.py --input pii_counts.json --source claims-2026 --pii-types ssn,age,zipcode,creditcard,email --output private.csv --scale 5.0 --threshold 10

In this example: 1. Scale 5.0: Adds significantly more noise than the default (2.0), resulting in a lower epsilon: 0.2 per PII type, so 1.0 for the five types in the JSON example above. 2. Threshold 10: Any PII count that, after adding noise, is less than 10 will be completely masked as None.
